newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE'S METKA POSTS STRONG H1, SEES GOOD PROSPECTS.
newsitem.headline: GREECE'S METKA POSTS STRONG H1, SEES GOOD PROSPECTS.

text.p: Mechanical construction and engineering firm Metka said its first half pretax earnings rose 45.6 percent to 775 million drachmas on turnover growth of 40.3 percent at 8.672 billion.

"Metka's orderbook of signed contracts on September 11 stands at 28 billion drachmas. These projects will assure full capacity for 1997 but additional works are expected," board chairman Alexandros Koukolis told reporters.
"As it stands, 1997 will be another good year like 1996," he said.
Conservative estimates see 1996 pretax profit at 1.6 billion drachmas on turnover of at least 15 billion, 18 billion in 1997, company executives said.

Metka's technical capabilities are evidenced by the range of projects it has undertaken so far, including construction of steel towers for the Public Power Corporation (DEH), lignite grinding mills, handling conveyors and parts of hydroelectric power stations.

Along with generator rotors, turbine casings and electrostatic precipitators the company also specialises in heavy ship loading cranes. Presently, its fixed assets have a market value of 25 billion drachmas, executives said.
Metka enjoyed a strong balance sheet with practically no debt, self financing its needs for working capital and investments. Its cash reserves rose 73 percent to 1.63 billion in the first half.

The company is also developing new activities in after sales service, an area of specialised maintenance of DEH power plants which on average have an age of around 20 years. These were being serviced exclusively by foreign operators.
The new activities have strong long term prospects and are already making up 15-20 percent of turnover.

"After sales service expands power plant capacity of DEH plants and employs Greek technical staff for work that used to be done by foreign specialist staff. It also prevents foreign currency outflows since service and upgrades now takes place in Greece," said managing director Andreas Anastasopoulos.

Metka which is also carrying out specialised projects for the Greek navy is also expecting work from two sizeable DEH projects -- a lignite plant in Florina budgeted at 180-200 billion drachmas and a 500 MW power plant in Komotini budgeted at 60 billion.
The projects are close to their final implementation stage and Metka is virtually sure of substantial subcontracting work.
The lignite unit in Florina which has been awarded to Gasprom-Promitheus could bring 15-20 billion drachmas of additional business, executives said.

"We should note that so far there hasn't been one single lignite station built in Greece without the direct or indirect involvement of Metka. A good example is the St. Demetrios unit being built by the Ansaldo-Waagner Biro-Aegek consortium," Anastasopoulos said.
"Metka is delivering work in this project worth 15 billion drachmas." Metka is also eyeing work from Canada's TVX Gold investment in northern Greece, he said.

Shares of Metka have been trading very actively on the Athens stock exchange. They have rallied from around 2,900 last week to close at 3,355 drachmas on Wednesday on heavy volume of 102,690 shares. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
